rv.q: After this, the musical comes alive. Much of it is down to the leads: Fraser plays a sulky, tyrannical, overgrown schoolboy but steers away from cardboard characterisation. So does Ibe, who makes a thoroughly impressive professional debut in the role.
The whiff of creating a eugenics-inspired master race by other means clings to it, so too agitprop induced brainwashing, the Republic of Gilead also hoving into view.

How fortunate for an ordinary man to have such a fantastic theatre just a short walk away from the street where he lives. Terrible puns aside, this is a simply exceptional production of the musical theatre classic My Fair Lady, featuring stunning costumes, hilarious performances, thrilling choreography and cock-e-nay accents galore.
